title: Work Unit - STRICT profile (normative + one canonical form per field)
description: NORMATIVE profile plus: exactly one shape per field (no union), a sentinel that starts with the SUCCESS: terminal-state marker, and no undeclared properties. This is the profile NEW units must be authored against; it is deliberately stricter than the existing corpus so that the union shapes the corpus already contains are visible as a finite, countable migration debt rather than as an invisible norm.

assigned_model_vendor_role.$comment: canonical: the object form. The 'model/vendor/role' slash-triple string (128 units) is machine-splittable but loses the optional basis/rationale field and cannot carry a value containing '/'.

tests_required.$comment: canonical: an array, so each required test is individually addressable by a runner. 96 units carry a single prose string instead.

failure_classification.$comment: canonical: an array of class tokens, so a failure can be classified by set membership. 96 units carry a prose string instead.

completion_sentinel.$comment: AGENTS.md 4 terminal-state discipline: the sentinel opens with SUCCESS:<unit-id>. Whether the id it names is its OWN id is a cross-field rule (SEM-002) that JSON Schema cannot express.

$comment: unevaluatedProperties:false composes over the whole allOf chain and rejects a misspelled field (e.g. 'dependencie'). TWO draft-2020-12 annotation facts make this subtle, both measured rather than assumed. (1) It only works because the structural profile omits `additionalProperties` - setting it to `true` would annotate every unknown property as evaluated and silently neutralise this keyword. (2) When the referenced normative profile FAILS, its annotations are discarded, so every property becomes unevaluated and this keyword also reports a violation at <root>. That secondary report is a CASCADE, not an independent unknown-property finding; wfdsl.validate reports strict failures that already fail normative separately so the cascade is never miscounted as a typo.
